scope: Improve qualified Bayer boundaries with original unreconstructed green clipping and measured R/B. No language rewrite; HL5, X-Trans and calibration unchanged. Legacy retained; D40 and postponed point 6 excluded.
decision: Installed dir5 after numerical, native XPC, full-image, export and GUI checks. Removes a documented local legacy advantage on boundary peak error. Does not establish general superiority: legacy still wins other regions and texture/full-clipping comparisons.

method.cause: An affine surface requires independent spatial support for its slopes. A thin border strip can lack that support even when every original colour sample lies on a bit-exact constant surface. Directional green/colour-difference interpolation then creates false colour.
method.admission: Existing dir4 first; otherwise exact two-level surfaces in 13x13, >=3 sites per side/channel, >=10% contrast, common monotone non-axial boundary. Only original green clipping on the bright side; R/B and dark side original, no recovered evidence. Intermediate sample values, noise/texture, R/B or multi-channel clipping rejected.
method.censored_green: Only missing channels change. Dark-side and R/B predictions use observed constants; bright-side missing green is the closest linear working RGB to the existing autonomous directional estimate under fixed R/B and green>=observed clipped plateau. Scaled matrix, f64 accumulations and finite fp32 check. Neither LibRaw matching nor assumed neutral. The projection property only applies when the true colour lies on the admitted ray; not a calibrated scene guarantee.
method.preservation: Every supplied CFA value retained; valid RAW untouched. No RGB clamp, denoising, extra raster, allocation or changed memory plan; local mask/counters within existing 8 KiB reserve. Recipe/cache now dir5; frozen dir4 equations and old calibration maintained for comparators.

native_comparison.limits: Counts refer to regional metric comparisons, not independent scenes. Overlapping regions and CFA phases correlated. Known-model matrices also generate truth. Chroma can be unbounded for signed RGB with small sum; no DeltaE. No general superiority or physical camera calibration claim. Common populations are explicitly recomputed for each pair; do not compare their scores across pairs as if the pixel sets were identical. Main boundary example uses fixed-region RGB maximum.

photographic_limits: Eight reused complete inputs and 400 remosaics from 25 reused photos unchanged bit-for-bit. No new measured photographic/noise improvement claimed; these are regression controls, not calibrated independent camera truths.

performance.scope: Paired full decoder in one executable, cal2/dir4 versus cal2/dir5. Same input/WB/native geometry, 3 warmups then 30 alternating pairs, identical opt-level=3 and thin LTO. Input read and output hashing excluded; allocation/parse/unpack/HL/demosaic/matrix included. No concurrent build/test/GUI/campaign. OS activity, thermals and cold start not controlled. This is not a new LibRaw timing comparison.

checks.initial_GUI_attempt: Timeout at 55 seconds without captures during concurrent full RAW verification; retained in verify.log. Entire verify.sh --gui rerun alone succeeded on a fresh private root; release GUI also passed.

open: Legacy remains locally better on other edges, texture and completely clipped highlights, including the inner patch of the same demonstrated boundary scene.
Projection and constant-surface admission remain assumptions from sparse CFA samples; aliasing or unseen chromatic variation are not excluded.
Ten previously tracked HL2 peak comparisons on seven scenes remain unchanged; this is a follow-up, not a fresh exhaustive HL2 comparison.
Previous native D750 comparisons against LibRaw showed slower autonomous rendering; the current timing only checks dir5 versus dir4.
Measured photographic targets, sensor clipping calibration, LED/spectral characterization, broader independent noisy photography, RSS under pressure and global release gates remain open.

Final synthetic verification contains 696 nonconstant signals plus 112 ambiguity controls, 750 unique RAW hashes. Two additional ramp/step pairs share the RAW because the step is hidden by clipping; phases, overlapping regions and generator families are correlated, and compatibility matrices also generate truth. Normalized signed-RGB chromaticity is not DeltaE.
